content: The content provided appears to be a detailed list of references and data related to tuberculosis (TB) research, including studies on latent TB infection (LTBI), active TB, and various diagnostic and treatment strategies. 1. The Temprano ANRS 12136 trial evaluated long-term outcomes and was published in The Lancet Global Health in 2017, highlighting the impact of early antiretroviral therapy and isoniazid preventive therapy in resource-limited settings. 2. Bruins and van Leth conducted a systematic review in 2017 (Infectious Diseases) to assess the effect of secondary preventive therapy on TB recurrence in individuals living with HIV, emphasizing the importance of tailored interventions. 3. Gupta et al. (2007, Clinical Infectious Diseases) studied postpartum TB incidence and mortality among HIV-infected women and their infants in Pune, India, between 2002 and 2005, revealing significant risks in this population. 4. Bothamley (2001, Drug Safety) reviewed the safety considerations of TB drug treatment during pregnancy, providing critical insights into maternal and fetal health. 5. The World Health Organization (WHO) updated its 2015 recommendations on 36 months of isoniazid preventive therapy for adults and adolescents living with HIV in high TB and HIV prevalence settings, emphasizing its programmatic importance. 6. Zar et al. (2007, BMJ) conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effect of isoniazid prophylaxis on mortality and TB incidence in children with HIV, demonstrating its life-saving potential. 7. Madhi et al. (2011, New England Journal of Medicine) investigated primary isoniazid prophylaxis in HIV-exposed children, showing its effectiveness in reducing TB risk. 8. Gray et al. (2014, International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease) piloted isoniazid preventive therapy in HIV-infected children on antiretroviral therapy, highlighting its feasibility and benefits. 9. Frigati et al. (2011, Thorax) examined the combined impact of isoniazid preventive therapy and antiretroviral therapy on TB in HIV-infected children in high-incidence settings, demonstrating significant reductions in TB incidence. 10. The WHO's 2016 consolidated guidelines on antiretroviral drug use for HIV treatment and prevention provided a public health approach to managing HIV and TB co-infection. 11. Getahun et al. (2011, PLoS Medicine) developed a standardized TB screening rule for people living with HIV in resource-constrained settings, based on a meta-analysis of observational studies. 12. The WHO's 2016 guidance on chest radiography for TB detection summarized current recommendations and programmatic approaches for its use in TB diagnosis. 13. Cranmer et al. (2016) evaluated the performance of the WHO TB symptom screen in hospitalized HIV-positive Kenyan children, presented at the 47th World Conference on Lung Health. 14. van ’t Hoog et al. (2013) systematically reviewed the sensitivity and specificity of symptomand chest radiography-based screening for active pulmonary TB in HIV-negative individuals and those with unknown HIV status. 15. Mulenga et al. (2015, Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal) assessed the role of clinical symptoms in diagnosing intrathoracic TB in young children, emphasizing the need for accurate diagnostic tools. 16. Kruk et al. (2008, Pediatrics) demonstrated the feasibility of symptom-based screening for child TB contacts in resource-limited settings, improving early detection. 17. Triasih et al. (2015, Clinical Infectious Diseases) prospectively evaluated symptom-based screening for managing children in contact with TB cases, showing its utility in high-burden settings. 18. Mandalakas et al. (2013, Thorax) modeled the cost-effectiveness of strategies to prevent TB in child contacts in high-burden settings, supporting targeted interventions. 19. Rangaka et al. (2012, The Lancet Infectious Diseases) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the predictive value of interferon-gamma release assays for incident active TB. 20. Mahomed et al. (2011, PLoS One) compared the tuberculin skin test and QuantiFERON-TB Gold in predicting TB disease in an adolescent cohort in South Africa. 21. Mathad et al. (2016, American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine) explored cytokine responses associated with latent TB test discordance in HIV-infected pregnant women. 22. McCarthy et al. (2015, International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease) reported a high incidence of latent TB infection among South African healthcare workers, calling for urgent action. 23. Sharma et al. (2017, PLoS One) compared the tuberculin skin test and interferon-gamma release assays for diagnosing latent TB infection in high-burden settings. 24. Dorman et al. (2014, American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine) evaluated interferon-gamma release assays and tuberculin skin testing for latent TB diagnosis in U.S. healthcare workers. 25. Zwerling et al. (2011, PLoS Medicine) developed the BCG World Atlas, a database of global BCG vaccination policies and practices. 26. Zennner et al. (2017, Annals of Internal Medicine) updated a network meta-analysis on the treatment of latent TB infection, providing evidence for optimal regimens. 27. Comstock (1999, International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease) examined the required isoniazid dosage for TB prevention in immunocompetent adults. 28. Den Boon et al. (2016, AIDS) reviewed continuous isoniazid use for latent TB treatment in people living with HIV. 29. Stagg et al. (2014, Annals of Internal Medicine) conducted a network meta-analysis on latent TB treatment, comparing various regimens. 30. Galli et al. (2016, International Journal of Molecular Sciences) analyzed pediatric TB epidemiology and clinical data from the Italian Pediatric TB Register. 31. Spyridis et al. (2007, Clinical Infectious Diseases) compared 9-month isoniazid monotherapy with shorter isoniazid-rifampin regimens for latent TB treatment in children. 32. van Zyl et al. (2006, International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease) studied adherence to anti-TB chemoprophylaxis and treatment in children. 33. Martinson et al. (2011, New England Journal of Medicine) evaluated new regimens to prevent TB in adults with HIV infection. 34. Sterling et al. (2016, AIDS) assessed a 3-month weekly rifapentine and isoniazid regimen for latent TB treatment in HIV-co-infected individuals. 35. Villarino et al. (2015, JAMA Pediatrics) tested a 3-month, 12-dose rifapentine-isoniazid regimen for TB prevention in children and adolescents. 36. Moro et al. (2016, American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine) analyzed pregnancy safety of rifapentine-isoniazid regimens versus daily isoniazid. 37. Belknap et al. (2017, Annals of Internal Medicine) compared self-administered versus directly observed rifapentine-isoniazid treatment for latent TB. 38. Balcells et al. (2006, Emerging Infectious Diseases) examined the risk of resistant TB with isoniazid preventive therapy. 39. Den Boon et al. (2016, International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease) reviewed rifampicin resistance after latent TB treatment. 40. Podany et al. (2015, Clinical Infectious Diseases) studied efavirenz pharmacokinetics in HIV-infected individuals receiving rifapentine-isoniazid. 41. Weiner et al. (2014, Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy) investigated rifapentine-raltegravir pharmacokinetic interactions in healthy volunteers. 42. Sotgiu et al. (2015, European Respiratory Journal) reviewed toxicity monitoring in latent TB treatment. 43. The WHO's 2017 guidelines addressed drug-susceptible TB treatment and patient care. 44. Garcia-Prats et al. (2014, International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease) investigated children exposed to multidrug-resistant TB in a daycare setting. 45. Trieiu et al. (2015, Emerging Infectious Diseases) evaluated moxifloxacin prophylaxis against MDR-TB in New York. 46. Bamrah et al. (2014, International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease) studied latent TB treatment in MDR-TB contacts in Micronesia. 47. Schaaf et al. (2002, Pediatrics) followed young children in contact with MDR-TB cases for 30 months. 48. The WHO's 2014 companion handbook provided guidance on managing drug-resistant TB. 49. The WHO's 2015 framework for active TB drug-safety monitoring emphasized implementation strategies. 50. Takizawa et al. (1999, Human & Experimental Toxicology) compared fluoroquinolone arthropathy in dogs. 51. Hempel et al. (1997, Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal) reported on ciprofloxacin use in pediatrics. 52. Warren (1997, Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal) discussed rheumatologic aspects of fluoroquinolone use in pediatric cystic fibrosis. 53. Denholm et al. (2015, International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease) explored ethical considerations in latent TB public health policy. 54. The WHO's 2017 ethics guidance supported the implementation of the End TB Strategy. 55. Kass (2001, American Journal of Public Health) proposed an ethics framework for public health. 56. Getahun et al. (2016, European Respiratory Journal) advanced global management of latent TB in at-risk populations.
